The truth is, reality is subjective.

I know, I know. "Facts are facts, empirically true and ambivolent to our perceptions of them." This is how I used to feel, but I've realized that it's not that simple.

The truth is, people are animals. We're just these creatures living on this planet. For the sake of this thought-experiment, it might be helpful to imagine humans as the bug aliens from starship troopers or something. Distance yourself from being a human for a moment, and really try to take an objective view of what humans are.

We don't actually "see", we have light sensors. We don't actually "hear", we have vibration sensors. We perceive certain stimulus and we mistake that for reality. In truth, none of us have ever, even for a second, actually perceived reality... All we get is this illusion of reality as reconstructed by our light sensors as interpreted by our brain. It's like the difference between a photograph and an oil painting. What we think is reality is actually an interpretation.

Once you understand this, everything else makes sense. You, and everyone else you know, are objectively living in different realities because you receive different stimulus and interpret that data in different ways. Imagine two blind people in separate rooms divided by a pane of sound-proof glass. That's what perception is like. You're in your world, I'm in mine, and we can never fully understand what the other person's world is like.

And the final factor, to really drive this home, is that people are emotional animals. Not only are our perceptions subjective, but the filter that processes information is tainted by how that information makes us feel. How often are people reluctant to accept blame for their actions? How often do people refuse to accept ways that they might be doing something wrong? That's all day, every day, everywhere. I mean, really, think about that for a moment. If a guy leaves the stove on, and it starts a fire, it will be harder for him to believe what happened if he's the one who left the stove on. The fact is, people's realities are monumentally distorted by choosing to believe or not believe things based on how those facts make them feel.

Take the phrase "refuse to believe". That's a phrase in the English language, and it's a totally real phenomena. People absolutely have the power to prevent a fact from permeating their belief system. If I say to my wife "you just refuse to believe that you're over-cooking the casserole" that's not just an idle statement. In that context I would literally be accusing her of being unwilling to incorporate a fact into her reality.

So, in a world where perceptions are subjective and emotions distort reality, is there any wonder that people sometimes believe bullshit.

Of course, as we all know, we're the exceptions. My reality is a perfectly constructed unbiased objective view of reality. It's only OTHER people who have this problem with complicating their reality with biased or mistake information... Right?

And that's the tricky part. As obvious as it is that other people are wrong, it's almost impossible to fathom that our perceptions could be (probably are) just as distorted with our own subjective bullshit.

In your world, and in mine, homeopathic medicine is obviously bullshit. In their world, traditional medicine is bullshit. I choose to believe the science that says homeopathic medicine is an absolute farce. They choose to believe that the science that says it's a farce is bullshit.

That's life. That's humanity. It's the chickens running the chicken coup. We're just a bunch of science monkeys run amok, with no supervision of any authority which could arbitrate any more enlightened understanding. And that's probably your answer for religeon too. With all of these flaws wih humans, the idea that there could be some infallible arbitrator of reality to watch over us is a nice thought, and as I've been saying this whole time, there's often little difference between a "nice thought" and a "fact".

Distance yourself from being a human for a moment, and really try to take an objective view of what humans are.

We don't actually "see", we have light sensors. We don't actually "hear", we have vibration sensors. We perceive certain stimulus and we mistake that for reality. In truth, none of us have ever, even for a second, actually perceived reality... All we get is this illusion of reality as reconstructed by our light sensors as interpreted by our brain. It's like the difference between a photograph and an oil painting. What we think is reality is actually an interpretation.

Once you understand this, everything else makes sense. You, and everyone else you know, are objectively living in different realities because you receive different stimulus and interpret that data in different ways. Imagine two blind people in separate rooms divided by a pane of sound-proof glass. That's what perception is like. You're in your world, I'm in mine, and we can never fully understand what the other person's world is like.

And the final factor, to really drive this home, is that people are emotional animals. Not only are our perceptions subjective, but the filter that processes information is tainted by how that information makes us feel. How often are people reluctant to accept blame for their actions? How often do people refuse to accept ways that they might be doing something wrong? That's all day, every day, everywhere. I mean, really, think about that for a moment. If a guy leaves the stove on, and it starts a fire, it will be harder for him to believe what happened if he's the one who left the stove on. The fact is, people's realities are monumentally distorted by choosing to believe or not believe things based on how those facts make them feel.

Take the phrase "refuse to believe". That's a phrase in the English language, and it's a totally real phenomena. People absolutely have the power to prevent a fact from permeating their belief system. If I say to my wife "you just refuse to believe that you're over-cooking the casserole" that's not just an idle statement. In that context I would literally be accusing her of being unwilling to incorporate a fact into her reality.

So, in a world where perceptions are subjective and emotions distort reality, is there any wonder that people sometimes believe bullshit.

Of course, as we all know, we're the exceptions. My reality is a perfectly constructed unbiased objective view of reality. It's only OTHER people who have this problem with complicating their reality with biased or mistake information... Right?

And that's the tricky part. As obvious as it is that other people are wrong, it's almost impossible to fathom that our perceptions could be (probably are) just as distorted with our own subjective bullshit.

In your world, and in mine, homeopathic medicine is obviously bullshit. In their world, traditional medicine is bullshit. I choose to believe the science that says homeopathic medicine is an absolute farce. They choose to believe that the science that says it's a farce is bullshit.

That's life. That's humanity. It's the chickens running the chicken coup. We're just a bunch of science monkeys run amok, with no supervision of any authority which could arbitrate any more enlightened understanding. And that's probably your answer for religeon too. With all of these flaws wih humans, the idea that there could be some infallible arbitrator of reality to watch over us is a nice thought, and as I've been saying this whole time, there's often little difference between a "nice thought" and a "fact".
